To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pro‐drug OTZ is a promising agent for increasing the efficacy and safety of chemotherapy with CY, a widely used anticancer drug.

OTZ decreases the GSH levels of B16 melanomas, sensitizing them in vitro and in vivo to the cytotoxic effects of CY, and increases the GSH levels, decreasing the toxicity and increasing the survival of mice treated with lethal dose of CY.
L‐2‐ oxothiazolidine4‐ carboxylate (an agent that increases glutathione levels) can be used as a protective agent against cyclophosphamideside effects in mice bearing B‐16 melanoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel therapeutic strategies based on the selective modulation of GSH levels in normal and tumour tissues to enhance the therapeutic benefit of CY in the treatment of metastatic melanoma.
the use of OTZ to protect against alkylator‐induced immunotoxicity and to increase the antitumour efficacy of these drugs in mice bearing B 16 melanoma liver metastasis.
the development of new strategies to improve the therapeutic index of CY by combining this drug with OTZ, which selectively increases GSH levels in PBMCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OTZ is a promising agent to enhance CY‐induced cytotoxicity in melanoma and to reduce its toxic effects on PBMCs, thus improving the therapeutic benefit of CY in the treatment of B16 melanomas.
the use of OTZ as a GSH precursor in conjunction with CY may improve the therapeutic benefit of CY in the treatment of melanoma.

OTZ, in addition to its ability to decrease GSH content and proliferation in tumour cells, can also enhance the therapeutic efficacy of alkylating agents by protecting normal cells against the toxic action of these drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OTZ may have potential as a chemosensitizing agent in the treatment of melanoma.
OTZ is a promising drug for the treatment of melanoma, and it could be used to protect against alkylating agent‐induced immune suppression.
OTZ is a promising agent for the treatment of malignant tumours.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a prodrug of the cysteine donor L‐2‐ oxothiazolidine ‐4‐carboxylic acid in combination with cyclosphosphamide can increase the efficacy of chemotherapy in melanoma liver metastasis‐induced mouse models.
OTZ, a GSH‐precursor pro‐drug, may enhance the therapeutic benefit of CY, reducing its toxicity and increasing survival of mice bearing B16 melanoma.
the combination of OTZ and CY is a promising strategy for the treatment of malignant metastatic melanoma.
